# E159 -- NMAAHC

## Metadata
- **Organization:** National Museum of African American History and Culture (NMAAHC), Smithsonian Institution
- **Year:** 2019 (Version 1.0, June 2019)
- **Sector:** Museum / Cultural
- **Pages:** 50
- **Design Agency:** Not credited (internal, Office of Public Affairs)
- **Format Quality:** High; polished InDesign layout, letter-size landscape, well-structured TOC and section dividers

## Brand Strategy
Four institutional pillars: (1) repository for African American culture exploration, (2) helping all Americans see how their stories are shaped by global influences, (3) exploring what it means to be American through resilience/optimism/spirituality, (4) place of collaboration beyond D.C. Six brand values explicitly defined: Authenticity, Innovation, Discovery, Excellence, Resilience, Spirituality. Brand approach emphasizes consistent voice and character to build meaningful relationships with audiences. The guide is positioned as a living document -- "always a work in progress" -- designed to be flexible and functional for a vibrant cultural institution.

## Logo
- Three-tiered icon inspired by Yoruban crown art from West Africa (also mirrors museum architecture)
- Vertical and horizontal logo variants, plus color versions
- Text set in Freight typeface (replacing earlier Neutraface -- "pointy M" vs "squared-off M" test for old vs new)
- Lockup system: standalone, with Smithsonian logo, with tagline (never all three combined)
- Minimum size: 1.5" wide (horizontal), 0.75" wide (vertical)
- Clear space: relative to icon tiers (2 tiers for horizontal, 1 tier for vertical)
- May appear in black, brand purple, or white (reversed); entire design always one color
- Icon may be used alone only with OPA approval and only on social media / promo items
- Detailed misuse guidance: no stretching, no color changes, no rearrangement, no busy backgrounds, no shadows/effects
- Department lockups and partner co-branding system with clear primary/secondary hierarchy
- Sub-branding requires OPA approval; must use brand color and typography

## Typography
- **Primary family:** Freight (Text and Sans) by Joshua Darden (African American designer -- intentional cultural connection)
- Freight Text: serif, Light through Black (12 styles with italics)
- Freight Sans: sans serif, Light through Black (12 styles with italics)
- Expressive range encouraged: different weights/styles convey mood from celebratory to serious
- Detailed notes on numerals (lining vs oldstyle figures), punctuation (em dashes, en dashes, typographer's quotes, diacriticals)
- Fallback fonts: Calibri (sans), Minion or Palatino (serif) -- internal use only; all public-facing must use Freight
- Available via Adobe Fonts

## Color
**Primary palette:**
- NMAAHC Purple: Pantone P 90-15 C (CMYK 40/81/0/49, HEX #612A60) -- primary brand color, culturally significant (royalty, faith, prosperity, healing)
- White (#FFFFFF)
- Warm Gray: Pantone Warm Gray 8 C (#8C8279)
- Black (#000000)

**Supporting palette (18 colors in 6 hue families, each with dark/main/light):**
- Magenta: #89294C / #AD2F4D / #E5B1B9
- Red-Orange: #9E3D1F / #DA4926 / #F4B485
- Yellow: #B4841E / #EDA A1A / #FAD97F
- Green: #61713C / #8E9933 / #DAD78A
- Teal: #2F6460 / #1C8B81 / #9FCEC3
- Blue: #4B556F / #5D6D9C / #B6C0D8

Colors described as "rich, bold, and warm" -- neither super-saturated nor dull. Sample color combination examples provided with mood guidance. Supporting palette used for accents, color-coding, and visual interest. Tinting rules: only tint light shades, never main or dark shades.

## Graphics
- **Corona Pattern:** Derived from the museum building's lattice ironwork. Used as textural background element. Low-contrast application with large clear text overlay for legibility.
- No formal icon system or illustration guidelines documented.

## Photography
Comprehensive photography guidelines across 7 pages:
- Must embody brand values (authenticity, innovation, discovery, excellence, resilience, spirituality)
- People depicted respectfully and empoweringly, never objectifying
- **Interaction:** Include people being engaged in exhibitions/events wherever possible
- **Lighting:** Indirect natural light preferred; avoid fluorescent/flash; professional quality required
- **Human subjects:** Show faces, include names and context to humanize subjects
- **Historical images:** Use when relevant but balance with contemporary photography; museum is forward-looking
- **Collection objects:** Isolate from backgrounds where possible; always include artist/title/medium/date/acquisition info
- **Mood:** Match photo feeling to context; bright/sunny = positive, stark/subdued = powerful
- **Color and photography:** Use primary palette alongside photos; supporting colors for complement/contrast

## Applications
- Sample layouts across multiple formats: postcards, newsletters, event programs, posters, web ads, digital newsletters, book signing materials
- Layout principles documented: hierarchy, scale, focus
- File format specifications: EPS/vector for print (CMYK), PNG for web (RGB, 72ppi), PNG for PowerPoint (RGB, 96ppi)
- Clear checklist for branded communications (logo, CTA, date/time/location, contact/social info)

## Tone of Voice
Dedicated "Brand Voice" section (pages 9-11):
- Voice is authentic, inclusive, accessible, welcoming, respectful
- Tone spans a range: celebratory to serious, casual to formal -- context-dependent
- Avoids language too formal (exclusionary) or too casual (inaccessible)
- Style matrix with examples: celebratory (book reading), casual (concert announcement), formal (memorial dedication), serious
- Social media may be more casual
- "Amplify voices" directive: use quotations from audiences, experts, and primary sources
- Writing samples provided as concrete examples
- Specific naming convention: full name "National Museum of African American History and Culture" preferred, no ampersand; "NMAAHC" only where necessary
- Respect and inclusion: use empowering, respectful, inclusive terminology; recognize evolving identity language

## Outliers
- Cultural intentionality in every design decision: Yoruban-inspired icon, African American type designer, culturally significant purple
- Corona pattern derived directly from physical architecture creates unique tangible-to-digital brand bridge
- Accessibility and inclusion section (page 49) with concrete guidelines -- rare in brand guides of this era
- Unusually detailed punctuation and numeral guidance for a brand guide
- The "old vs new logo" identification test (pointy M vs squared-off M) is a pragmatic migration tool

## Quality Score
**4.5 / 5** -- Exceptionally well-structured guide covering all major brand dimensions with depth and intentionality. Brand strategy is clearly articulated through pillars and values. Typography and color sections are thorough with practical usage guidance. Photography guidelines are among the most detailed seen in museum brand guides. Tone of voice section provides both principles and concrete examples. Minor gaps: no formal grid/layout system beyond principles, no motion/animation guidelines, and the corona pattern could use more application examples. The cultural intentionality woven throughout elevates this beyond a standard identity manual.
